papers.title_en: C$^3$PO: Evaluating Cross-Modal Composition and Counterfactual Performance in Omnimodal Models
papers.authors: Swapnanil Mukherjee, Agyeya Negi, Tanuja Ganu, Ponnurangam Kumaraguru
papers.evidence: 提出评估跨模态组合与反事实冲突的基准，针对多模态推理脆弱性，属于稳健多模态学习工具
papers.tldr: 多模态大模型虽能处理多种输入，但推理常偏向单一模态，导致跨模态推理脆弱。为此提出C^3PO基准，包含3404个样本，通过25个逻辑模板自动构建，评估信息组合与反事实冲突能力。结果显示人类准确率88.64%，最佳模型Gemini-3.1-Pro仅73.17%，且86-95%失败源于模态主导，注意力集中于文本。该基准揭示跨模态推理缺陷，强调架构需支持持续跨模态注意力。
papers.abstract_en: Current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can process diverse sensory inputs, yet their reasoning remains heavily biased toward a dominant modality, resulting in brittle cross-modal reasoning. We introduce C$^3$PO, a benchmark of 3,404 samples spanning video, audio, image, and text, evaluating two abilities: information composition (fusing dispersed evidence) and counterfactual conflict (resolving deliberate contradictions). C$^3$PO's paired IC/CC structure and four-tier design enable targeted diagnosis of when and why cross-modal reasoning fails. Built through a fully automatic pipeline using 25 logically grounded templates, C$^3$PO reveals that while humans achieve 88.64% accuracy, the best model (Gemini-3.1-Pro) reaches only 73.17%, with open-source models collapsing under conflict. Through attention probes, we find 86-95% of failures stem from modality dominance: models commit to one modality while ignoring contradictory evidence, concentrating 87-95% of attention on text. Mid-layer attention entropy predicts correctness-sustained exploration succeeds, premature collapse fails. The 56-point accuracy gap between equally complex templates reveals that performance depends on modalities' structural roles in conflict resolution, not combinations. These findings show multimodal perception does not guarantee robust reasoning; architectures must enable sustained cross-modal attention to avoid premature

papers.title_en: Local Margin Restoration for Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
papers.authors: Yan Huang, Guowei Wang, Xu Wang, Kangjun Liu, Xin Lin
papers.evidence: 面向视觉语言模型的鲁棒测试时自适应
papers.tldr: 视觉语言模型在测试时遇到分布偏移性能会急剧下降，现有测试时自适应方法因top-1式更新损坏类别间局部语义结构，且迭代过程不断积累偏差，最终导致模式崩溃。针对这些耦合问题，我们提出轻量的一步式局部边缘恢复（LMR）框架：在样本级用受保护边缘恢复（PMR）屏蔽外部硬负样本以重建局部几何，在流级用自适应边缘（AM）控制器与偏置校正（BC）动态阻止偏差累积。在CIFAR-C、ImageNet-C及ImageNet变体上，LMR始终优于现有最优方法，尤其在低批次测试场景下展现出极强的鲁棒性和高效性。该工作为视觉语言模型的可靠测试时自适应提供了全新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) such as CLIP exhibit remarkable zero-shot capabilities, yet their performance frequently degrades sharply under unexpected test-time distribution shifts. While Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) offers a promising solution, continuously adapting VLMs over an unlabeled test stream presents fundamental challenges. Conventional top-1-centric updates often reinforce errors by corrupting the local semantic geometry among related classes, while iterative adaptation exacerbates progressive bias accumulation, ultimately driving the model toward mode collapse. To overcome these coupled vulnerabilities, we propose Local Margin Restoration (LMR), a lightweight, one-step TTA framework. At the sample level, our Protected Margin Restoration (PMR) objective recovers local semantic geometry by shielding plausible near-top candidates from external hard negatives. Concurrently, to combat stream-level degradation, we introduce a dual-stage stabilization mechanism, featuring an Adaptive Margin (AM) controller and Bias Correction (BC), to dynamically disrupt progressive bias accumulation and prevent mode collapse. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-C, ImageNet-C, and ImageNet variants demonstrate that LMR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art TTA baselines, proving exceptionally robust and efficient even in challenging low-batch test-time regimes. Our code is available at https://github.com/DennisHuangYan/LMR.

papers.title_en: Multimodal Alignment Through Joint Kernel Entropic Gromov--Wasserstein Optimal Transport
papers.authors: Yixuan Florence Wu, Yilun Zhu, Naichen Shi
papers.evidence: 面向共享潜在空间的结构保持多模态对齐，在配对数据稀缺时为鲁棒融合提供方法支持。
papers.tldr: 多模态对齐在配对数据稀缺时挑战巨大，现有方法基于原始特征距离易破坏结构。本文提出JK-EGW框架，基于模态内外细粒度相似性构建全局亲和核，通过联合核熵Gromov-Wasserstein最优传输对齐预训练嵌入。理论上给出n^{-1/2}样本复杂度，算法上以低秩近似与变分提升实现可扩展求解。实验验证其在多模态检索上优于现有基线，为数据稀缺场景提供有效方案。
papers.abstract_en: We study the problem of aligning data from multiple modalities into a shared representation space, focusing on settings where strong pretrained unimodal encoders are available but cross-modal paired data are scarce. We propose a structure-preserving alignment framework, joint kernel entropic Gromov--Wasserstein Optimal Transport (JK-EGW), which maps multiple modalities into a common latent space by minimizing a quadratic optimal transport objective. JK-EGW leverages fine-grained similarity relationships within and across modalities to construct a global affinity kernel instead of relying on raw feature-space distances. Our framework naturally provides explicit control over the geometry and distribution of the latent embedding. On the theory side, we establish parametric sample complexity rate of $n^{-1/2}$, matching the corresponding rates for standard, entropic and Gromov--Wasserstein optimal transport. On the algorithmic side, we derive a scalable alternating procedure to solve JK-EGW with entropic optimal transport (EOT) updates through a low-rank kernel approximation and a variational lifting. This lifting scheme effectively relieves the burden of a quadratic objective, and allowing us to take the advantage of existing EOT solvers. Empirically, we focus on post-hoc alignment of embeddings from pretrained encoders in data-scarce regimes, and show that our proposed method achieves improved multimodal retrieval performance compared to existing alignment baselines.
